source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a spherical mirror is concave or convex from the way its reflecting surface curves.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: spherical mirror is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use the reflecting surface, not the shaded non-reflecting surface, to name the mirror.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Use the reflecting surface, not the shaded non-reflecting surface, to name the mirror is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: A spherical mirror with a reflecting surface curving inwards is concave; a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface curving outwards is convex. reflecting surface curvature determines mirror type The learner classifies a spherical mirror by the curvature of its reflecting surface: inward is concave and outward is convex. A curved mirror can be named from whichever side looks hollow, even if that side is the shaded non-reflecting surface.
